intro: You've searched for a virtual bookkeeper near me, which tells us you want bookkeeping help that works around your life, without the need to visit an office. Perhaps you're self-employed, running a small business from home, or simply too busy to keep on top of receipts and invoices. We introduce you to UK bookkeepers who work remotely, and they'll quote you directly for the help you need.
need_heading: What people searching for a virtual bookkeeper usually need
need_lead: Most people looking for a virtual bookkeeper want someone who can take the paperwork off their hands and work with the tools they already use.
needs: You run a small business or work for yourself and your receipts, invoices and bank statements have piled up because you've been too busy earning.
You want a bookkeeper who can work remotely using cloud accounting software, so you're not tied to someone local or expected to drop off paperwork.
You need help setting up or tidying your bookkeeping system, including connecting bank feeds and choosing a receipt-capture app.
You're unsure how to keep your records in order for HMRC and want someone to show you a simple, reliable routine.
You'd like to hand over the day-to-day bookkeeping but still understand what's going on, with clear communication and agreed response times.
context_heading: What to understand about virtual bookkeeping
context: Virtual bookkeepers work remotely, often through cloud software, bank feeds and document apps, so location matters less than you might think. That said, bookkeeping is not a regulated title in the UK, but anyone providing bookkeeping services for a fee must be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, either by HMRC or by a professional body. Membership of the Institute of Certified Bookkeepers (ICB) or the Association of Accounting Technicians (AAT) shows a bookkeeper has trained to a recognised standard and agreed to a code of conduct.

Ask whether a bookkeeper holds professional indemnity insurance and which body supervises them. Good bookkeepers are also clear about where their work stops and an accountant's starts, for example on year-end accounts and tax advice. Because they work remotely, you should also agree how they will access your records and how that access will be removed if you stop working together.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Describe the type of business you run and whether you're a sole trader, partnership or limited company.
Say which cloud accounting software you use, if any, and whether you're happy to move to a different system.
Mention how many transactions or records you deal with in a typical month, so the bookkeeper can gauge the work involved.
Explain whether you need help with a backlog of records or ongoing bookkeeping support.
State whether you want the bookkeeper to work alongside an accountant and where you see the boundaries.
Let us know your preferred way of communicating, such as email, phone or video calls, and any times you're usually available.
questions_heading: Questions to ask a virtual bookkeeper
questions: Which receipt-capture tools do you use, and how do they work with my existing software?
How do you prefer to communicate, and what response times can I expect?
How will you access my financial records, and how is that access removed if we stop working together?
Which body supervises you for anti-money-laundering purposes, and do you hold professional indemnity insurance?
Where does your work stop and an accountant's begin, for example on year-end accounts and tax advice?
Can you help me set up bank feeds and a simple routine for keeping records up to date?

faqs.q: Do I need a bookkeeper who is physically near me if they work virtually?
faqs.a: Not usually. Virtual bookkeepers work remotely through cloud software, bank feeds and document apps, so location matters less. What matters more is that you're comfortable with their tools and communication style.

faqs.q: Is bookkeeping a regulated profession in the UK?
faqs.a: Bookkeeping is not a regulated title in the UK, but anyone providing bookkeeping services for a fee must be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, either by HMRC or by a professional body. Membership of the Institute of Certified Bookkeepers (ICB) or the Association of Accounting Technicians (AAT) shows a bookkeeper has trained to a recognised standard and agreed to a code of conduct.

faqs.q: How do virtual bookkeepers keep my financial data secure?
faqs.a: They typically use cloud accounting software with secure logins and may ask you to grant access rather than share passwords. You should ask how access is granted and removed, and whether they use receipt-capture apps that store documents securely.

faqs.q: Can a virtual bookkeeper help if I'm behind with my records?
faqs.a: Yes, many will help you catch up on a backlog before moving to ongoing support. Be clear about how far behind you are and whether you need one-off help or regular bookkeeping.
